# Zendesk

Connect your own Zendesk user after choosing its site in the native account connection form.
The host validates one Zendesk subdomain, freezes its HTTPS origin on the account, and uses that
origin for authorization, callback, saved grant, refresh, health and API credential placement.
Tool input and catalog query parameters cannot retarget an account. The catalog source remains
available without optional hosted client credentials.

`currentUser`, `listTickets`, and `getTicket` run without approval. `createTicket` always requires
approval. Health reads `/api/v2/users/me.json` with the caller's account.

## OAuth

A pre-existing compatible public client lets a person consent without creating an OAuth client
or entering a secret. Confidential BYO remains available under Advanced. BYO is an advanced
fallback; requiring end-user client registration does not meet site-plus-sign-in onboarding.
The host keeps client secrets and rotating refresh tokens. The declaration uses PKCE S256 and
JSON token requests. Public clients use `none`; clients with a secret use `client_secret_post`.
The requested scopes are `tickets:read tickets:write users:read`.

A public integration distributed across customer companies must satisfy Zendesk's publisher
registration and Marketplace requirements. An existing client does not establish approval,
global-client status or cross-company eligibility. The internal-company exception is separate.

The catalog can populate `integrationHeaders` in `configuration.ts` with assigned publisher
metadata: `X-Zendesk-Marketplace-Name`, `X-Zendesk-Marketplace-Organization-Id` and
`X-Zendesk-Marketplace-App-Id`. Those are public metadata, not credentials. No IDs are fabricated.
The app sends configured headers on every API request, including health. Token-endpoint header
applicability and live provider approval remain separate acceptance checks.

## Framework and evidence

This private source pins `apps@0.0.1-beta.104-basalt.1` from the prepared host. Community
publication requires checks against the chosen public host and an approved publisher scope.
Two mocked sites can prove routing and refresh; that evidence does not establish live Zendesk
consent, registration, Marketplace approval or unrelated-company acceptance.
